gate_rule_as_set: proceed only if V2 reproduces the board materially better than V1 does
stopped_at: Part 3; no pre-registration frozen, no arm trained, no submission built
why_fail: V2 is FURTHER from the board than V1 on ST-RAE under all three window rules (0.1361 against 0.1573-0.2256).

V2's only clear per-isoform gain is CYP2C9, measured here as the isoform with essentially no activity-based selection (AUC 0.596) and therefore the one the premise predicts least benefit for. The gain is in the wrong place for the mechanism.

CYP2D6's V2 ST-RAE is not identified: it spans 0.8153-1.6046 across three defensible window rules, with the board's 1.1673 inside that range. A window exists that reproduces the board, but choosing it for that reason is fitting the answer.
V2's CYP1A2 ST-RAE is 1.0010 -- this project's reference model is no better than predicting the mean on that surface, which is not a board-like surface.
what_the_gate_does_NOT_establish: It does not refute the TRAINING claim. The external report makes two separable claims: that adding interval rows to TRAINING is worth -0.243 macro ST-RAE, and that an interval VALIDATION SURFACE reproduces the board. The gate tested only the second. The first is untested here and remains open.

It does not say the interval labels are wrong, only that a surface built from them does not track the board -- which is expected once measured, because the board's population is curve-bearing compounds and V2's is mostly screened-only compounds with bands 1.8-8.7x wider than a real credible interval.
what_IS_established_and_is_stronger_than: CYP2D6 promotion is a hard activity threshold: log2FC < -0.613 classifies it at 99.57% against a 65.9% base rate, AUC 0.9998. The external claim reproduces exactly, as does its ~2,883 count (2,882 measured).

The promotion rule is NOT the same on the other three isoforms, which was not quoted anywhere: CYP1A2 AUC 0.896 (biased, not a cut), CYP2C9 0.596 (near-independent), CYP3A4 0.411 (INVERTED -- less-inhibitory compounds more likely promoted).

CYP2D6's no-inhibition interval window cannot be calibrated from this project's own data at all: zero promoted compounds carry a no-inhibition readout, and 2,648 of its 2,882 excluded compounds (91.9%) fall in that bin.

The model IS mis-calibrated on the excluded population, measured without any fitted window: 66.4% of CYP2D6's confirmed non-inhibitors are predicted above the assay's own detection limit, against 43.2% / 18.4% / 8.8% for CYP1A2 / CYP2C9 / CYP3A4 -- an ordering IDENTICAL to the ordering of selection strength.
cheapest_decisive_next_test_NOT_run_here: The training claim can be tested without the V2 surface at all: train arm A (CYP2D6 interval rows added) against notebook 37's existing mae_only arm on the frozen partition, and score it on the UNCHANGED V1 surface -- curve-bearing compounds only, identical cells. If the premise's diagnosis is right, fixing the training population should improve the model on the dose-response population too, because a model that stops over-predicting non-inhibitors should rank the weak end better. That is one arm (~4-6 h), not two, needs no interval window on the scoring side, and so is immune to everything the gate just rejected. Not run here: the task's rule was to stop at a failed gate, and starting a 6 h run against it is not this notebook's call to make.
assay_condition_caveat: UNVERIFIED-HERE: the brief states the single-concentration screen is the TDI/+NADPH condition, not the scored direct-inhibition condition. Nothing in this repository records the file's assay condition, and the no-fetch rule forbids retrieving the dataset card. If true, every interval label here rests on an adjacent assay, which would weaken the training claim too, not just the surface.
